_note: Each eval carries an `assertions` array. Every assertion has a `tier`: 'deterministic' assertions are executed by evals/run_evals.py — it runs scan_usage.py / target_options.py against the fixture and checks a JSON path, no network, no LLM, CI-safe. 'llm_graded' assertions describe a rewrite-quality criterion a grader applies to the skill's output; each may also carry `staticChecks` (file-scoped substring/regex tests the runner evaluates deterministically when a --with-skill output tree is supplied). Each eval also carries an optional `platform` field ('android' | 'ios', default 'android') that the runner passes through to scan_usage.py and target_options.py — needed because the detection matrices and version catalogs are platform-scoped. See evals/README.md for the check-DSL and the with-skill vs baseline flow.

checkOps._doc: Operators usable in a deterministic assertion's `check.op`.
checkOps.ne: value at path does not equal expected
checkOps.notContains: string/list at path does not contain expected
checkOps.subset: expected list is a subset of the list at path
checkOps.setEq: list at path equals expected as a set
checkOps.in: value at path is one of expected (a list)
checkOps.hasKey: dict at path has expected key
checkOps.lengthEq: list/dict/string at path has length == expected
checkOps.regex: string at path matches expected regex

evals.name: full-android-migration
evals.prompt: We're stuck on an ancient version of the Salesforce Marketing Cloud SDK and upgrading has been a nightmare. Can you migrate our Android app to the latest SDK? The repo is at REPO_PATH. Update the code, the build.gradle, and the manifest, and tell me what I need to check by hand.
evals.expected_output: Scans repo, detects legacy MarketingCloudSdk 7.4.2 -> SFMCSdk 11.0.1. Rewrites init to SFMCSdk.configure, getInstance() calls to async requestSdk{}, setContactKey->identity.setProfileId, trackPageView->EventManager.customEvent+SFMCSdk.track. Flags addTag (tags) and the custom FirebaseMessagingService for manual review. Bumps build.gradle to sfmcsdk+pushfeaturemodule 11.0.1 (keeps marketingcloudsdk engagement module). Removes legacy manifest service. Preserves business logic (AnalyticsCache.lastUser, AppState.sdkReady, handleOwnPush). Produces a migration report.

assertions.description: Detects the legacy umbrella version 7.4.2.
Classifies the project as legacy (no unified core artifact present).
Migration status is not-started for a pure-legacy project.
Confirms an SFMC SDK module is actually integrated.
No unified sfmcsdk core artifact in a legacy project.
Sees the legacy MarketingCloudSdk.init/getInstance entry points.
Detects both core and push features in use.
Finds the init-sdk call site.
Finds the setContactKey identity call site.
Finds the trackPageView analytics call site.
The addTag call is flagged for manual review (>=1 manual-review finding).
Latest stable target is 11.0.1.
A legacy project is not already-current.
Reaching 11.0.1 crosses the architecture boundary (full code migration).
A partial target 'v10' expands to the newest 10.x release (10.0.0).
The legacy init is rewritten to SFMCSdk.configure with an SFMCSdkModuleConfig.build block, and setSenderId is moved onto the push feature config (not deleted).
assertions.rubric: The single MarketingCloudSdk.init(...) call is replaced by SFMCSdk.configure(context, SFMCSdkModuleConfig.build { ... }, listener). Engagement setters (setApplicationId/setAccessToken/setMarketingCloudServerUrl/setMid/setInboxEnabled/setAnalyticsEnabled/setNotificationCustomizationOptions) remain on an engagementModuleConfig MarketingCloudConfig; setSenderId is migrated onto a pushFeatureModuleConfig PushFeatureConfig (never dropped). The init-status callback body preserving AppState.sdkReady is retained.

assertions.description: setContactKey/setAttribute migrate to SFMCSdk.requestSdk { identity.edit { profileId = ...; attributes.set(...) } }; addTag is flagged, not silently dropped; AnalyticsCache.lastUser is preserved.
assertions.rubric: The registration edit chain is rewritten onto the unified identity API: profileId is set as a property (profileId = email), attributes go through attributes.set/put, all inside SFMCSdk.requestSdk { it.identity.edit { ... } }. The lambda uses the implicit extension receiver (no explicit named editor param) and there is no commit() call. The addTag(segment) call is either preserved on the engagement registrationManager or surfaced in the manual-review section — never silently deleted. The business line AnalyticsCache.lastUser = email survives unchanged.

assertions.description: The app-owned FirebaseMessagingService stays app-owned; only the two SDK calls inside it are rewritten onto PushFeature.requestSdk, and handleOwnPush is preserved.
assertions.rubric: The class remains a FirebaseMessagingService subclass owned by the app (not deleted, not replaced by an SDK class). setPushToken and handleMessage are routed through PushFeature.requestSdk { it.getPushMessageManager()... } (the async push entry point, not MarketingCloudSdk.getInstance()). PushMessageManager.isMarketingCloudPush stays a static call and its import moves to com.salesforce.marketingcloud.pushfeature.push. The customer's handleOwnPush path and its NotificationRouter.show call are preserved unchanged.

assertions.description: Gradle keeps the marketingcloudsdk engagement module and adds sfmcsdk + pushfeaturemodule; it does NOT remove marketingcloudsdk.
assertions.rubric: The dependency block still declares com.salesforce.marketingcloud:marketingcloudsdk (now the engagement feature module, kept — not removed) and adds com.salesforce.marketingcloud:sfmcsdk and com.salesforce.marketingcloud:pushfeaturemodule (push is in use). Versions may be the resolved runtime versions or the matrix seed fallback; sfmcsdk must NOT be pinned to 11.0.1 (no such artifact version on its stream).

assertions.description: The hand-declared legacy notification service is removed (auto-merged by the v11 push module).
assertions.rubric: The manual <service> declaration pointing at com.salesforce.marketingcloud.notifications.NotificationOpenedService is removed, because the unified push module auto-merges its own notification components. The app's own MainActivity and non-SDK manifest entries are untouched.

assertions.description: A migration report is produced covering summary, changes by area, manual-review items, and verification.
assertions.rubric: A migration report is generated (any reasonable filename) with: a from/to summary (legacy 7.4.2 -> unified 11.0.1), changes grouped by area with file:line, a 'Needs manual review' section that names the addTag tag handling and the custom FirebaseMessagingService, and a verification section with the build result and manual dev checks.

evals.name: full-ios-migration
evals.prompt: We're on a very old Salesforce Marketing Cloud iOS SDK and need to modernize. Can you migrate our iOS app to the latest unified SDK? The repo is at REPO_PATH. Update the Swift code, the Podfile, the entitlements, and the Notification Service Extension, and tell me what I need to verify by hand.
evals.expected_output: Scans repo, detects legacy MarketingCloudSDK 8.1.1 -> unified SFMCSDK 11.0.0. Rewrites sfmc_configure to SFMCSdk.initializeSdk driven by SFMCSdkConfigBuilder.setPush(config: PushConfigBuilder...), sfmc_setContactKey/sfmc_setAttributeNamed to SFMCSdk.identity, sfmc_trackPageView to SFMCSdk.track(event:), sfmc_setDeviceToken to SFMCSdk.mp.setDeviceToken, sfmc_setNotificationRequest to SFMCSdk.mp.setNotificationRequest. Flags the sfmc_addTag call and the Notification Service Extension for manual review. Bumps Podfile to MarketingCloudSDK 11.0.0 + SFMCSDK 4.0.0. Preserves AppState.sdkReady, AnalyticsCache.lastConfigureSucceeded, AppState.lastNotificationIdentifier. Produces a migration report.

assertions.description: Detects the legacy umbrella version 8.1.1 (from Podfile.lock + Podfile).
Classifies as legacy (no unified SFMCSDK core in Podfile.lock).
Migration status is not-started for a pure-legacy project.
Confirms an SFMC SDK module is actually integrated.
No unified SFMCSDK core artifact in a legacy project.
Sees the legacy MarketingCloudSDK.sharedInstance / sfmc_configure entry points.
Detects both core and push features in use (setDeviceToken + NSE).
Finds the sfmc_configure init call site.
Finds the sfmc_setContactKey identity call site.
Finds the sfmc_setDeviceToken push registration call site.
The NSE and the addTag call are flagged for manual review (>=2 findings).
Latest stable target is 11.0.0.
A legacy iOS project is not already-current.
Reaching 11.0.0 crosses the architecture boundary (full code migration).
sfmc_configure is rewritten to SFMCSdk.initializeSdk with SFMCSdkConfigBuilder.setPush and PushConfigBuilder, and AppState.sdkReady is preserved.
assertions.rubric: The MarketingCloudSDK.sharedInstance().sfmc_configure(with:) call is replaced by SFMCSdk.initializeSdk(...) driven by SFMCSdkConfigBuilder().setPush(config:onCompletion:) with a PushConfigBuilder that carries appId/accessToken/marketingCloudServerUrl/mid/inboxEnabled/analyticsEnabled. The AppState.sdkReady and AnalyticsCache.lastConfigureSucceeded assignments survive (possibly moved into the completion handler). The import switches to `import SFMCSdk` (MarketingCloudSDK import may remain for engagement types).

assertions.description: sfmc_setContactKey and sfmc_setAttributeNamed migrate to the unified SFMCSdk.identity API; sfmc_trackPageView migrates to SFMCSdk.track(event:); AnalyticsCache.lastUserEmail is preserved.
assertions.rubric: The three sfmc_setContactKey / sfmc_setAttributeNamed calls are rewritten onto SFMCSdk.identity (setProfileId / setProfileAttributes). The sfmc_trackPageView call migrates to SFMCSdk.track(event:) with a CustomEvent (initializer failability handled — no force-unwrap). The AnalyticsCache.lastUserEmail = email line survives unchanged. No legacy sharedInstance() calls remain in this file.

assertions.description: sfmc_setDeviceToken migrates to SFMCSdk.mp.setDeviceToken and sfmc_setNotificationRequest migrates to SFMCSdk.mp.setNotificationRequest; AppState.lastNotificationIdentifier is preserved.
assertions.rubric: MarketingCloudSDK.sharedInstance().sfmc_setDeviceToken(deviceToken) is rewritten to SFMCSdk.mp.setDeviceToken(deviceToken). MarketingCloudSDK.sharedInstance().sfmc_setNotificationRequest(request) is rewritten to SFMCSdk.mp.setNotificationRequest(request). The AppState.lastNotificationIdentifier assignment in the UN delegate survives. UNUserNotificationCenter delegate wiring is preserved.

assertions.description: The Podfile keeps MarketingCloudSDK (engagement module) and adds SFMCSDK (unified core); versions move to the v11 stream.
assertions.rubric: The Podfile still declares pod 'MarketingCloudSDK' (kept — this is the engagement module in v11, not removed) at ~> 11.0.0 (or a resolved 11.x pin). It ADDS pod 'SFMCSDK' at ~> 4.0.0 (or a resolved 4.x pin). It does NOT pin SFMCSDK to the 11.x stream (there is no such artifact). The MCExtensionSDK pod may also appear if the NSE Podfile target is present.

assertions.description: The Notification Service Extension is either flagged for manual review or migrated onto MCExtensionSDK — never silently rewritten with main-app SDK calls.
assertions.rubric: The NSE is treated with care. Either (a) the file is left with a clear manual-review marker/comment pointing at MCExtensionSDK and the required App Group entitlement, or (b) it is rewritten to use MCExtensionSDK (import MCExtensionSDK; SFMCSdkExtension or MCExtensionSDK equivalent) inside the NSE target only, NEVER by dropping in a plain SFMCSdk.mp call sourced from the main-app config. The core forwarding of the UNNotificationRequest to fetch attachments must remain.

assertions.description: A migration report is produced covering summary, changes by area, manual-review items, and verification.
assertions.rubric: A migration report is generated (any reasonable filename) with: a from/to summary (legacy 8.1.1 -> unified 11.0.0), changes grouped by area with file:line, a 'Needs manual review' section that names the sfmc_addTag call and the Notification Service Extension migration to MCExtensionSDK, and a verification section covering `pod install --repo-update` and a device push round-trip.
